title: Azure Functions: rolling updates are now generally available on Flex consumption.
summary: Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan now supports rolling updates for zero-downtime deployments. This feature gradually replaces instances instead of restarting all at once, allowing in-progress executions to complete and maintaining availability during deployment.
key_points: Rolling updates drain instances in small batches and scale out new instances with updated code to maintain capacity
Feature is only available on Flex Consumption plan, not on Consumption or Premium plans
Requires backward-compatible changes since old and new instances run together briefly during deployment
Comparison shows deployment slots on other plans don't guarantee zero downtime like rolling updates do

quotes.text: Instead of restarting everything at once, with this feature active the platform now replaces instances gradually.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core mechanism of rolling updates that enables zero-downtime deployments

quotes.text: Your changes need also to be backward compatible.
quotes.why_it_matters: Critical constraint for using rolling updates since old and new versions run concurrently

quotes.text: If you need true continuity for long-running or critical functions, rolling updates on Flex Consumption is the only option that delivers it today.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies when rolling updates are necessary versus when simpler strategies suffice
